lesson.title: Meeting the Letter T — and Blending Our First Word!
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You know S, M, and A. Today we meet one more letter, T — and then something exciting: we're going to blend sounds together into a real word for the first time!

The letter T makes a quick, tapping sound: t. Say it together, like a tiny tap of your tongue. Now for the exciting part: say the sounds /s/, /a/, /t/ one at a time, then say them faster and faster until they blend into a word: sss...aaa...t... sat! That's blending — putting individual sounds together to read a whole word.
You just read your very first word by blending sounds: sat! This is exactly how reading works — sound by sound, then blended together.

objectives: Identify the letter T and produce its most common sound (/t/)
Blend three individual sounds (/s/, /a/, /t/) into the word 'sat', a foundational decoding skill
materialsNeeded: Optional: letter cards or tiles for S, A, T if available
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce T and its sound: a quick tap, 't'.
2. Say a few T words together (top, tap, ten), listening for the sound at the start.
3. Review all four letters learned this week: S, M, A, T — say each sound in a row.
4. Model blending: say /s/, /a/, /t/ slowly, then faster, until it becomes 'sat'. Do this together several times.
5. If you have letter cards, physically slide S, A, T together while blending, to make the connection visual.
6. Move to the worksheet: trace the letter T, then practice blending 'sat' again.
7. Close by celebrating — the child just read their first word!
differentiationTips: Struggling: it's completely fine if blending doesn't click immediately — keep practicing /s/-/a/-/t/ slowly without rushing to the blended word
Ready for more: try blending a second word if the letters allow it (e.g. 'mat' using M, A, T)
For a child who enjoys hands-on learning, physically moving letter cards together while blending makes the abstract process concrete
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and blending-practice activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct letter formation and successfully blending 'sat'.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Blending individual letter sounds into a whole word is the pivotal Kindergarten decoding skill that everything in phonics builds toward — this lesson is the payoff for the whole week's letter-sound work.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.
